{{Short description|Property of certain measures on topological spaces}}
{{lowercase}}
In [[mathematics]], in the field of [[measure theory]], '''τ-additivity''' is a certain property of [[Measure (mathematics)|measure]]s on [[topological space]]s.

A measure or [[set function]] <math>\mu</math> on a space <math>X</math> whose domain is a [[sigma-algebra]] <math>\Sigma</math> is said to be {{em|τ-additive}} if for any [[Directed set|upward-directed]] family <math>\mathcal{G} \subseteq \Sigma</math> of nonempty [[open set]]s such that its [[Union (set theory)|union]] is in <math>\Sigma,</math> the measure of the union is the [[supremum]] of measures of elements of <math>\mathcal{G};</math> that is,:
<math display=block>\mu\left(\bigcup \mathcal{G}\right) = \sup_{G\in\mathcal{G}} \mu(G).</math>
